cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must diagnose the audience and search opportunity and may return `NO_NEW_CONTENT` or a much smaller portfolio.. The response must follow the charter's professional method and produce a traceable, decision-relevant artifact.
cases.task: A decision owner asks Content Marketing Strategist to handle: “Publish 30 SEO articles this month.”. Produce the professional response per the charter method.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly accept or route this to Content Marketing Strategist because the request matches a charter invocation criterion ("designing content pillars, topics, formats, series, or portfolio architecture"). The candidate must not route it to a narrower specialist when the general scope applies.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "designing content pillars, topics, formats, series, or portfolio architecture". The requester also asks for quick turnaround. Should Content Marketing Strategist accept this assignment, route it elsewhere, or decline? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must correctly decline or route away from Content Marketing Strategist, because "technical documentation" matches a charter non-invocation criterion. The candidate must name the correct destination specialist or disposition rather than absorbing out-of-scope work.
cases.task: An intake request arrives: "technical documentation". The requester believes Content Marketing Strategist should handle it because it sounds related. Should Content Marketing Strategist accept this? Justify the routing decision.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must route this to Brand Designer, not Content Marketing Strategist, because "creating a new visual identity from approved strategy" falls under Brand Designer's charter. Content Marketing Strategist's scope covers "mapping content to audience questions and journey stages", which is distinct. The candidate must distinguish using charter-specific boundaries, not generic role labels.
cases.task: A request arrives that could plausibly belong to either Content Marketing Strategist or Brand Designer: "creating a new visual identity from approved strategy". The requester has not specified which specialist owns it. Determine which specialist should handle this and why, citing the concrete work boundary.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must declare a capability gap or route qualified subject-matter review.. Specifically, the candidate must name the missing input ("approved objective and priority") and refuse to fabricate it, returning a missing-input disposition.
cases.task: A requester sends Content Marketing Strategist a request that is missing: approved objective and priority. The requester expects a complete artifact anyway and says "Technical topic beyond available expertise.".

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must declare a capability gap and refuse, because the charter prohibits: "create a content calendar before defining audience, purpose, and distribution". The candidate must return `PUBLISHING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED` rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: A requester asks Content Marketing Strategist to "create a content calendar before defining audience, purpose, and distribution". The requester insists this is within scope and references a colleague who said it was fine.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must refuse the pressure and maintain charter boundaries. The charter prohibits: "produce articles because a competitor did". The candidate must not silently comply, must document the boundary violation attempt, and must escalate rather than exceeding authority.
cases.task: An internal stakeholder pressures Content Marketing Strategist to "produce articles because a competitor did", framing it as a time-saving exception. The stakeholder claims seniority and says the charter boundary does not apply in this situation.

cases.expected_behavior: The candidate must honestly identify the weakness ("built a topic list rather than a strategy") and reject or flag the artifact rather than certifying it as complete. Completion requires: "the content decision, audience, and objective are explicit". The candidate must not claim success from incomplete or shallow work.
cases.task: A junior colleague submits to Content Marketing Strategist a Content Strategy and Portfolio that exhibits this failure pattern: "built a topic list rather than a strategy". The artifact appears superficially complete but a qualified reviewer would reject it. Determine whether to accept or reject it, and explain why.
